ordered_diagnoses: Hemorrhagic rectal ulcer due to anticoagulation

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute rectal bleeding with recent diarrhea in a postoperative patient
salient_findings: Multiple episodes of bright red blood per rectum
Circumferential wall thickening of the distal rectum with surrounding inflammatory change
Multiple, punched-out, irregular, nonbleeding ulcers in the rectum
key_facts: Recent coronary artery bypass graft surgery
Multiple episodes of bright red blood per rectum
No abdominal pain, rectal pain, melena, fevers, or chills

shortlist: Hemorrhagic rectal ulcer due to anticoagulation

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Viral cytopathic inclusions and CMV immunostain positive

shortlist.label: Ischemic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and dual antiplatelet therapy

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
shortlist.why_kept: Active colitis with ulcer and crypt distortion

shortlist.label: Diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Circumferential wall thickening of the distal rectum and surrounding inflammatory change

shortlist.label: Hemorrhagic rectal ulcer due to anticoagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Dual antiplatelet therapy and recent coronary artery bypass graft surgery

raw.rationale: Viral cytopathic inclusions highlighted by CMV immunostain and active colitis with ulcer, crypt distortion, and reactive changes support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Ischemic colitis
rejected.why: No evidence of ischemia, and recent coronary artery bypass graft surgery does not directly relate to colitis

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.why: Lack of chronic symptoms and absence of typical inflammatory bowel disease findings on histopathology

rejected.label: Diverticulitis
rejected.why: No diverticula mentioned, and symptoms do not align with typical diverticulitis presentation

rejected.label: Hemorrhagic rectal ulcer due to anticoagulation
rejected.why: While patient is on dual antiplatelet therapy, the presence of viral cytopathic inclusions and active colitis points towards an infectious cause
